title.zh: 卷十八 志第十 祥瑞
title.raw: 卷十八 志第十 祥瑞 Volume 18 Treatises 10: Auspicious Signs

sentences.zh: 天符瑞命，遐哉邈矣。

translations.literal: Heavenly talismans and auspicious mandates — how distant and far.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's talismans and the mandate of good omens — how far they recede into the past.

sentences.zh: 靈篇祕圖，固以蘊金匱而充石室，炳契決，陳緯候者，方策未書。

translations.literal: Spiritual chapters and secret charts were stored in golden caskets and filled the stone archives; those that clarify contracts and set forth omens were not yet written in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred texts and hidden charts lay sealed in golden chests and stone vaults; the writings that bind fate and read the heavens were not yet set down in the annals.

sentences.zh: 啓覺天人之期，扶獎帝王之運，三五聖業，神明大寶，二謀協贊，罔不由茲。

translations.literal: They awaken the season when Heaven and man align, bolster the fortune of emperors and kings; the sage undertakings of the Three and Five, the great treasure of the spirits — when two plans work together, nothing fails to proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: They rouse the hour when Heaven and humanity meet, lift the destiny of throne and crown; the holy work of the Three and Five, the gods' great heirloom — when counsel and omen move as one, every rise begins here.

sentences.zh: 夫流火赤雀，實紀周祚，雕雲素靈，發祥漢氏，光武中興，皇符爲盛，魏膺當塗之讖，晉有石瑞之文，史筆所詳，亦唯舊矣。

translations.literal: The Fire Star and red sparrow truly recorded Zhou's fortune; carved clouds and white spirits brought omens to Han; Guangwu's restoration made the imperial talisman supreme; Wei received the prophecy of holding the road; Jin had the stone omen text — what the historians detail is only the old pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The Fire Star and crimson sparrow marked Zhou's reign; cloud-carved omens and white spirits blessed Han; at Guangwu's revival the royal talisman shone brightest; Wei answered the prophecy of the road held; Jin answered the stone oracle — the brush has told it all, and the tale is old.

sentences.zh: 齊氏受命，事殷前典。

translations.literal: When the Qi house received the mandate, they followed the earlier model of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi took Heaven's charge, it kept the ancient rites of Yin.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎蘇偘撰《聖皇瑞應記》，永明中庾溫撰《瑞應圖》，其餘衆品，史注所載。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Su Kan compiled Records of the Sage Emperor's Auspicious Responses; in Yongming Yu Wen compiled Chart of Auspicious Responses; the rest are recorded in historical notes.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kan of the Yellow Gate wrote Records of the Sage Emperor's Auspicious Responses; in Yongming, Yu Wen wrote the Chart of Auspicious Responses; other items appear in the historians' notes.

sentences.zh: 今詳錄去取，以爲《志》云。

translations.literal: Now we select and record in detail to make this Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: What follows is chosen and set down in full as this Treatise.

sentences.zh: 《老子河洛讖》曰：「年曆七七水滅緒，風雲俱起龍麟舉。

translations.literal: The Laozi River Chart Prophecy says: 「Seven sevens in the year tally — water extinguishes the thread; wind and clouds rise together, dragons and qilin ascend.
translations.idiomatic: The Laozi River Chart Prophecy reads: 「Seven sevens in the years' count — water puts out the line; wind and cloud lift as one, dragon and qilin rise.

sentences.zh: 」宋水德王，義熙十四年，元熙二年，永初三年，景平一年，元嘉三十年，孝建三年，大明八年，永光一年，泰始七年，泰豫一年，元徽四年，昇明三年，凡七十七年，故曰七七也。

translations.literal: 」Song was the Water Virtue dynasty: fourteen years of Yixi, two of Yuanxi, three of Yongchu, one of Jingping, thirty of Yuanjia, three of Xiaojian, eight of Daming, one of Yongguang, seven of Taishi, one of Taiyu, four of Yuanhui, three of Shengming — seventy-seven years in all; hence 「seven sevens.」
translations.idiomatic: 」Song held the Water Virtue: Yixi 14, Yuanxi 2, Yongchu 3, Jingping 1, Yuanjia 30, Xiaojian 3, Daming 8, Yongguang 1, Taishi 7, Taiyu 1, Yuanhui 4, Shengming 3 — seventy-seven years altogether, hence 「seven sevens.」

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「雲從龍，風從虎。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: 「Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: 「Clouds obey the dragon; wind obeys the tiger.

sentences.zh: 」關尹云：「龍不知其乘風雲而上天也。」

translations.literal: 」Lord Guan said: 「The dragon does not know it rides wind and clouds to ascend heaven.」
translations.idiomatic: 」Lord Guan said: 「The dragon does not know it mounts wind and cloud to reach heaven.」

sentences.zh: 讖又曰：「肅草成，道德懷書備出身，形法治吳出南京。

translations.literal: The prophecy also says: 「Sober grass completes; the Way and Virtue hold the book, ready to emerge — by form and law govern Wu, go forth from the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy adds: 「Sober grass is made whole; the Way and Virtue cradle the book and step forth — by form and statute rule Wu, issue from the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 」上卽姓諱也。

translations.literal: 」"Above" is the tabooed surname.
translations.idiomatic: 」"Above" stands for the imperial clan name by taboo.

sentences.zh: 南京，南徐州治京口也。

translations.literal: Southern Capital is Jingkou, seat of Southern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Capital is Jingkou, where Southern Xuzhou was administered.

sentences.zh: 讖又曰：「墥堨河梁塞龍淵，消除水災泄山川。

translations.literal: The prophecy again says: 「The granary dike and river bridge block the dragon abyss; water disasters are cleared, mountains and rivers are opened.
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy again: 「Granary rampart and river span dam the dragon deep; the flood is drained, hills and streams released.

sentences.zh: 」墥堨河梁，爲路也，路卽道也。

translations.literal: 」"Granary dike and river bridge" mean a road; road is the Way.
translations.idiomatic: 」"Granary dike and river bridge" spell a road — and road is the Way.

sentences.zh: 淵塞者，譬路成也。

translations.literal: 「Abyss blocked」 — like the road made complete.
translations.idiomatic: 「Abyss blocked」 — as when the road is finished.

sentences.zh: 卽太祖諱也。

translations.literal: That is the Founding Emperor's taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: That points to the Founding Emperor's tabooed name.

sentences.zh: 消水災，言除宋氏患難也。

translations.literal: 「Eliminate water disaster」 means removing the Song house's calamities.
translations.idiomatic: 「Clear the water plague」 means clearing the Song dynasty's woes.

sentences.zh: 讖又曰：「上參南斗第一星，下立草屋爲紫庭。

translations.literal: The prophecy again says: 「Above, align with the first star of the Southern Dipper; below, a thatched hut stands as the Purple Court.
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy again: 「Above, take the Southern Dipper's first star; below, a grass hut serves as the Purple Court.

sentences.zh: 神龍之崗梧桐生，鳳鳥舒翼翔且鳴。

translations.literal: On the divine dragon's ridge wutong grows; the phoenix spreads its wings, soars, and cries.
translations.idiomatic: On the ridge of the spirit dragon the parasol tree rises; the phoenix spreads its wings, flies, and calls.

sentences.zh: 」南斗第一星，吳分也。

translations.literal: 」The first star of the Southern Dipper — Wu's astrological allotment.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Southern Dipper's first star — Wu's celestial share.

sentences.zh: 草屋，蕭字也。

translations.literal: Thatched hut — the character Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: 「Grass hut」 — the graph Xiao.

sentences.zh: 又簫管之器，像鳳鳥翼也。

translations.literal: Also the xiao pipe among instruments — like the phoenix's wings.
translations.idiomatic: The xiao flute, too, among the eight tones — shaped like the phoenix wing.

sentences.zh: 讖又曰：「蕭爲二士，天下大樂。

translations.literal: The prophecy again says: 「Xiao is two 「shi」 — great joy under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy again: 「Xiao splits into two 「shi」 — all under heaven rejoices.

sentences.zh: 」二士，主字也。

translations.literal: 」Two shi — the character for 「lord.」
translations.idiomatic: 」Two 「shi」 — the graph for 「lord.」

sentences.zh: 讖又曰：「天子何在草中宿。

translations.literal: The prophecy again says: 「Where is the Son of Heaven? Lodging in the grass.
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy again: 「Where does the Son of Heaven dwell? He lodges in the grass.

sentences.zh: 」宿，肅也。

translations.literal: 」"Lodging" — sober, submissive (su).
translations.idiomatic: 」"Lodging" (su) — sober (su), in the name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 《尚書中候儀明篇》曰：「仁人傑出，握表之象，曰角姓，合音之于。

translations.literal: The Shangshu Zhonghou, Yiming Chapter, says: 「An outstanding humane man, grasping the chart-image, called the Angular surname; combined sound 「yu」 「yu」.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangshu Zhonghou, Yiming Chapter, says: 「A humane man of rare stature holds the chart-sign — the Angular surname; its sounds joined read 「yu」 「yu」.

sentences.zh: 」蘇偘云：「蕭，角姓也。

translations.literal: 」Su Kan said: 「Xiao is the Angular surname.
translations.idiomatic: 」Su Kan said: 「Xiao is the Angular surname.

sentences.zh: 又八音之器有簫管也。」

translations.literal: Also among the eight tones is the xiao pipe.」
translations.idiomatic: And among the eight tones there is the xiao flute.」

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：案晉光祿大夫何禎解音之于爲曹字，謂魏氏也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Examining Jin Grand Master of Splendid Service He Zhen, who interpreted the combined sound 「yu」 「yu」 as the character Cao, meaning the Wei house —
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes: Jin's Grand Master of Splendid Service He Zhen read the joined sounds 「yu」 「yu」 as the graph Cao — the house of Wei —

sentences.zh: 王隱《晉書》云：「卯金音于，亦爲魏也。

translations.literal: Wang Yin's Jin Shu says: 「Mao-jin [Liu] with sound 「yu」 — again means Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin's Jin Shu says: 「Mao-jin [Liu] sounded with 「yu」 — again Wei.

sentences.zh: 」《候》書章句，本無銓序，二家所稱，旣有前釋，未詳偘言爲何推據。

translations.literal: 」The chapter-lines of the Hou book originally had no commentary order; both schools' claims already had prior explanations — it is unclear on what basis Su Kan's statement rests.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Hou text's lines were never ordered by commentary; both readings had older glosses — on what grounds Su Kan argued is not made plain.

sentences.zh: 《孝經鉤命決》曰：「誰者起，視名將。

translations.literal: The Xiaojing Gouming Jue says: 「Who shall rise? Look to the name Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaojing Gouming Jue says: 「Who will rise? Read the name Jiang.

sentences.zh: 」君者羣也，理物爲雄，優劣相次以期興，將，太祖小諱也。

translations.literal: 」「Jun」 means multitude; ordering things makes one heroic; ranks succeed, anticipating rise — 「Jiang」 is the Founding Emperor's childhood taboo.
translations.idiomatic: 」「Jun」 is the flock; he who orders things is chief; worth ranks in turn until the age turns — 「Jiang」 was the Founding Emperor's childhood taboo.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍蕭思話見之曰：「此我家諱也。」

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Xiao Sihua saw it and said: 「This is my family's taboo name.」
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua, General Who Pacifies the West, read it and said: 「That is my clan's taboo name.」

sentences.zh: 王子年歌曰：「金刀治世後遂苦，帝王昏亂天神怒，災異屢見戒人主，三分二叛失州土，三王九江一在吳，餘悉稚小早少孤，一國二主天所驅。

translations.literal: Wang Zinian's song says: 「The golden blade rules the age, then comes bitter hardship; emperors and kings grow dim, Heaven's god is wrathful; disasters appear again and again warning the ruler; two of three parts rebel, territories lost; three kings at Jiujiang — one in Wu; the rest all young, orphaned early; one state, two lords — Heaven drives them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zinian's song runs: 「The golden blade governs the world, then bitterness follows; thrones darken and Heaven's lord grows wroth; omens crowd the sky to warn the king; two of three turn traitor, provinces slip away; three kings at Jiujiang — one in Wu; the rest are children, orphaned young; one realm, two masters — Heaven drives them on.

sentences.zh: 」金刀，劉也。

translations.literal: 」"Golden blade" — Liu.
translations.idiomatic: 」"Golden blade" — the Liu house.

sentences.zh: 三分二叛，宋明帝世也。

translations.literal: 「Two of three rebel」 — the age of Emperor Ming of Song.
translations.idiomatic: 「Two of three in revolt」 — the reign of Song Mingdi.

sentences.zh: 三王九江者，孝武於九江興，晉安王子勛雖不終，亦稱大號，後世祖又於九江基霸迹，此三王也。

translations.literal: 「Three kings at Jiujiang」: Xiaowu rose at Jiujiang; Jin'an Prince Zixun, though he did not finish, also took a great title; later the Founding Emperor again laid his hegemonic base at Jiujiang — these are the three kings.
translations.idiomatic: 「Three kings at Jiujiang」: Emperor Xiaowu rose there; Prince Zixun of Jin'an, though he failed, still claimed the throne; later the Founding Emperor founded his rise at Jiujiang — these three kings.

sentences.zh: 一在吳，謂齊氏桑梓，亦寄治南吳也。

translations.literal: 「One in Wu」 — the Qi house's native soil, also governed from southern Wu.
translations.idiomatic: 「One in Wu」 — Qi's homeland, also ruled from southern Wu.

sentences.zh: 一國二主，謂太祖符運潛興，爲宋氏驅除寇難。

translations.literal: 「One state, two lords」 — the Founding Emperor's mandate rose in secret, driving out the Song house's enemies.
translations.idiomatic: 「One realm, two masters」 — the Founding Emperor's fortune stirred unseen, clearing Song's foes.

sentences.zh: 歌又曰：「三禾摻摻林茂孳，金刀利刃齊刈之。

translations.literal: The song again says: 「Three grain-stalks, thick and tangled, the forest lush with seed — the golden blade's sharp edge, Qi shall mow them.
translations.idiomatic: The song adds: 「Three stalks, thick in the grove, the woods heavy with grain — the golden blade's edge, and Qi will reap them down.

sentences.zh: 」刈，翦也。

translations.literal: 」"Mow" — to cut away.
translations.idiomatic: 」"Mow" — to cut away.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「實始翦商。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: 「Thus began the cutting of Shang.」
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: 「So began the shearing of Shang.」

sentences.zh: 歌又曰：「欲知其姓草肅肅。

translations.literal: The song again says: 「Would you know his surname? Grass, sober, sober.
translations.idiomatic: The song again: 「Would you know the clan name? Grass — sober, sober.

sentences.zh: 糓中最細低頭熟。

translations.literal: The finest grain in the heap bows its head, ripe.
translations.idiomatic: The finest grain in the bin bows its head, ripe.

sentences.zh: 鱗身甲體永興福。

translations.literal: Scaled body, armored form — eternal rising fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Scaled hide, armored flesh — fortune that endures and ascends.

sentences.zh: 」糓，道；

translations.literal: 」"Grain" — the Way;
translations.idiomatic: 」"Grain" — the Way;

sentences.zh: 熟，成：又諱也。

translations.literal: Ripe, accomplish: again a taboo name.
translations.idiomatic: “Ripe” means “accomplish”—and is again a taboo name.

sentences.zh: 太祖體有龍鱗，斑駮成文，始謂是黑歷，治之甚至而文愈明。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor’s body bore dragon scales, mottled into patterns; at first they were taken for black moles; treatment was applied to the utmost and the patterns grew clearer.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Progenitor’s body bore dragon scales, mottled into patterns. At first they were taken for black moles; treatment was pushed to the limit, and the markings only grew clearer.

sentences.zh: 伏羲亦鱗身也。

translations.literal: Fuxi too had a scaly body.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi too had a scaly body.

sentences.zh: 《金雄記》曰：「鑠金作刀在龍里，占睡上人相須起。

translations.literal: Record of the Golden Male says: 「Smelting gold to make knives in Dragon Hamlet; divining sleep, superiors and inferiors alike must rise.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of the Golden Male says: 「Smelting gold to make knives in Dragon Hamlet; divining sleep, superiors and inferiors alike must rise.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「當復有作肅入草。

translations.literal: 」It also says: 「There shall again be one who takes Su entering the grass.
translations.idiomatic: 」It also says: 「There shall again be one who takes Su entering the grass.

sentences.zh: 」蕭字也。

translations.literal: 」—the character Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: 」—the character Xiao.

sentences.zh: 《易》云：「聖人作之。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 「The sage made it.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: 「The sage made it.

sentences.zh: 」記又云：「草門可憐乃當悴，建號不成易運沸。

translations.literal: 」The Record also says: 「The grass gate is pitiful and about to wither; founding the title will not succeed—the dynasty’s turn boils.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Record also says: 「The grass gate is pitiful and about to wither; founding the title will not succeed—the dynasty’s turn boils.

sentences.zh: 」《詩》云不時，時也。

translations.literal: 」The Odes say “not timely”—it means timely.
translations.idiomatic: 」The Odes’ “not timely” means timely.

sentences.zh: 不成，成也。

translations.literal: “Not accomplished” means accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: “Not accomplished” means accomplished.

sentences.zh: 建號，建元號也。

translations.literal: “Founding the title” means founding the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: “Founding the title” means founding the reign title.

sentences.zh: 易運，革命也。

translations.literal: “Change the turn” means revolution.
translations.idiomatic: “Change the turn” means revolution.

sentences.zh: 武進縣彭山，舊塋在焉。

translations.literal: Peng Mountain in Wujin county—the ancestral tombs lay there.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Mountain in Wujin county—there lay the ancestral tombs.

sentences.zh: 其山崗阜相屬數百里，上有五色雲氣，有龍出焉。

translations.literal: Its ridges and mounds run on for several hundred li; five-colored cloud vapor appears above, and dragons emerge there.
translations.idiomatic: Its ridges and mounds run on for several hundred li; five-colored clouds gather above, and dragons appear there.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝惡之，遣相墓工高靈文占視，靈文先與世祖善，還，詭荅云：「不過方伯。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song hated this and sent the tomb geomancer Gao Lingwen to inspect. Lingwen had been on good terms with Shizu; on his return he answered deceitfully: 「No more than a regional lord.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song took alarm and sent the tomb geomancer Gao Lingwen to inspect. Lingwen had been friendly with Shizu; returning, he answered deceitfully: 「No more than a regional lord.

sentences.zh: 」退謂世祖曰：「貴不可言。

translations.literal: 」Privately he told Shizu: 「Your nobility is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: 」Privately he told Shizu: 「Your nobility is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」帝意不已，遣人於墓左右校獵，以大鐵釘長五六尺釘墓四維，以爲厭勝。

translations.literal: 」The emperor’s suspicion did not cease; he sent men to hunt by the tombs and drove great iron nails five or six feet long into the four corners of the tombs as averting magic.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor’s suspicion did not cease; he sent men to hunt beside the tombs and drove great iron nails five or six feet long into the four corners of the graves as averting magic.

sentences.zh: 太祖後改樹表柱，柱忽龍鳴，響震山谷，父老咸志之云。

translations.literal: Later the Grand Progenitor replaced the boundary marker posts; a post suddenly roared like a dragon, the sound shaking the valleys—all the elders recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Grand Progenitor replaced the boundary marker posts; a post suddenly roared like a dragon, the sound shaking the valleys—the elders all recorded it.

sentences.zh: 會稽剡縣刻石山，相傳爲名，不知文字所在。

translations.literal: Mount Keshi in Shan county, Kuaiji, is so called by tradition; where the writing lay was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Keshi in Shan county, Kuaiji, is so called by tradition; where the inscription lay was unknown.

sentences.zh: 昇明末，縣民兒襲祖行獵，忽見石上有文凡三處，苔生其上，字不可識。

translations.literal: At the end of Shengming, the county man Er Xiuzu went hunting and suddenly saw writing on the stone in three places; moss grew over it and the characters could not be made out.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shengming, the county man Er Xiuzu went hunting and suddenly saw writing on the stone in three places; moss covered it and the characters could not be read.

sentences.zh: 刊苔去之，大石文曰：「此齊者，黃公之化氣也。

translations.literal: They scraped away the moss; on the great stone it read: 「This Qi is the transformed vapor of the Yellow Duke.
translations.idiomatic: They scraped away the moss; on the great stone it read: 「This Qi is the transformed vapor of the Yellow Duke.

sentences.zh: 」立石文曰：「黃天星，姓蕭字某甲，得賢帥，天下太平。

translations.literal: 」On the standing stone: 「Yellow Heaven star; surname Xiao, given name so-and-so; obtaining a worthy commander, all under Heaven is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: 」On the standing stone: 「Yellow Heaven star; surname Xiao, given name so-and-so; obtaining a worthy commander, all under Heaven is at peace.

sentences.zh: 」小石文曰：「刻石者誰？

translations.literal: 」On the small stone: 「Who carved the stone?
translations.idiomatic: 」On the small stone: 「Who carved the stone?

sentences.zh: 會稽南山李斯刻秦望之封也。」

translations.literal: Li Si of Kuaiji’s southern mountains carved the Qin Prospect’s feng sacrifice.」
translations.idiomatic: Li Si of Kuaiji’s southern mountains carved the Qin Prospect’s feng sacrifice.」

sentences.zh: 益州齊后山，父老相傳，其名亦不知所起。

translations.literal: Qihou Mountain in Yizhou—the elders hand down the name, but its origin too is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Qihou Mountain in Yizhou—the elders hand down the name, but its origin too is unknown.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年，有沙門玄暢於山丘立精舍，其日，太祖受禪日也。

translations.literal: Shengming 3, the monk Xuan Chang built a monastery on the hillock—that day was the day the Grand Progenitor received the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Shengming 3, the monk Xuan Chang built a monastery on the hillock—that day was the day the Grand Progenitor received the abdication.

sentences.zh: 嵩高山，昇明三年四月，滎陽人尹午於山東南澗見天雨石，墜地石開，有璽在其中，方三寸。

translations.literal: Song Mountain: fourth month of Shengming 3, Yin Wu of Xingyang saw stones rain from heaven in the southeastern ravine; when they struck the ground the stone split open, and within was a seal three inches square.
translations.idiomatic: On Song Mountain, in the fourth month of Shengming 3, Yin Wu of Xingyang saw stones rain from heaven in the southeastern ravine; when they struck the ground a stone split open, and within was a seal three inches square.

sentences.zh: 其文曰：「戊丁之人與道俱，肅然入草應天符。

translations.literal: Its text read: 「A man of wu and ding walks with the Way; solemnly entering the grass, he answers Heaven’s talisman.
translations.idiomatic: Its inscription read: 「A man of wu and ding walks with the Way; solemnly entering the grass, he answers Heaven’s talisman.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「皇帝興運。

translations.literal: 」It also said: 「The emperor’s fortune rises.
translations.idiomatic: 」It also said: 「The emperor’s fortune rises.

sentences.zh: 」午奉璽詣雍州刺史蕭赤斧，赤斧表獻之。

translations.literal: 」Wu presented the seal to the Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Chifu; Chifu memorialized it as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wu presented the seal to the Inspector of Yongzhou Xiao Chifu; Chifu memorialized and presented it.

sentences.zh: 史臣案：昔大人見臨洮而銅人鑄，臨洮生董卓而銅人毀，有卓而世亂，世亂而卓亡，如有似也。

translations.literal: The historiographer notes: In old times, when the Grand Man appeared at Lintao, bronze men were cast; Lintao produced Dong Zhuo and the bronze men were destroyed—Dong Zhuo brought chaos to the age, chaos ended Dong Zhuo; the pattern here is much the same.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer notes: When the Grand Man appeared at Lintao, bronze men were cast; Lintao produced Dong Zhuo and the bronze men were destroyed—Dong Zhuo brought chaos, chaos ended Dong Zhuo; the parallel is close.

sentences.zh: 晉末嵩高山出玉璧三十二，宋氏以爲受命之祥。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, Song Mountain produced thirty-two jade bi; the Song house took this as an omen of receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jin, Song Mountain yielded thirty-two jade bi; the Song house took this as an omen of receiving the mandate.

sentences.zh: 今此山出璽，而水德云謝，終始之徵，亦有類也。

translations.literal: Now this mountain yields a seal, and the Water Virtue’s cycle is spent—omens of beginning and end show a similar type.
translations.idiomatic: Now this mountain yields a seal, and the Water Virtue’s cycle is spent—portents of beginning and end follow a similar pattern.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年，太祖從南郊，望氣者陳安寶見太祖身上黃紫氣屬天，安寶謂親人王洪範曰：「我少來未嘗見軍上有如此氣也。」

translations.literal: Yuanhui 4, the Grand Progenitor attended the southern suburb; the qi-gazer Chen Anbao saw yellow and purple vapor on his body reaching to Heaven. Anbao told his kinsman Wang Hongfan: 「From my youth I have never seen a commander with such aura.」
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhui 4, the Grand Progenitor attended the southern suburb; the qi-gazer Chen Anbao saw yellow and purple vapor on his person reaching to Heaven. Anbao told his kinsman Wang Hongfan: 「From my youth I have never seen a commander with such aura.」

sentences.zh: 太祖年十七，夢乘青龍西行逐日，日將薄山乃止，覺而恐懼，家人問占者，云「至貴之象也」。

translations.literal: At seventeen the Grand Progenitor dreamed he rode an azure dragon westward chasing the sun; as the sun neared the mountains he stopped. Waking in fear, his family asked a diviner, who said, 「A sign of the utmost nobility.」
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen the Grand Progenitor dreamed he rode an azure dragon westward chasing the sun; as the sun neared the mountains he stopped. Waking in fear, his family asked a diviner, who said, 「A sign of the utmost nobility.」

sentences.zh: 蘇偘云：「青，木色。

translations.literal: Su Kan said: 「Azure is the color of wood.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kan said: 「Azure is the color of wood.

sentences.zh: 日暮者，宋氏末運也。」

translations.literal: A setting sun means the Song house’s last turn.」
translations.idiomatic: A setting sun means the Song house’s last turn.」

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，明帝遣前淮南太守孫奉伯往淮陰監元會。

translations.literal: Taishi 7, Emperor Ming sent the former Administrator of Huainan Sun Fengbo to Huaiyin to oversee the year-end gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi 7, Emperor Ming sent the former Administrator of Huainan Sun Fengbo to Huaiyin to oversee the year-end gathering.

sentences.zh: 奉伯與太祖同寢，夢上乘龍上天，於下捉龍脚不得。

translations.literal: Fengbo slept with the Grand Progenitor and dreamed of riding a dragon up to Heaven; from below he grasped the dragon’s feet but could not hold them.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo slept with the Grand Progenitor and dreamed of riding a dragon up to Heaven; from below he grasped the dragon’s feet but could not hold them.

sentences.zh: 覺謂太祖曰：「兖州當大庇生民，弟不見也。

translations.literal: On waking he told the Grand Progenitor: 「Yan province will greatly shelter the people—you, younger brother, do not see it.
translations.idiomatic: On waking he told the Grand Progenitor: 「Yan province will greatly shelter the people—you, younger brother, will not see it.

sentences.zh: 」奉伯卒於宋。

translations.literal: 」Fengbo died in Song.
translations.idiomatic: 」Fengbo died in Song.

sentences.zh: 清河崔靈運爲上府參軍，夢天帝謂己曰：「蕭道成是我第十九子，我去年已授其天子位。

translations.literal: Cui Lingyun of Qinghe, a staff officer of the Chief Office, dreamed the Lord on High told him: 「Xiao Daocheng is my nineteenth son; last year I already granted him the Son of Heaven’s throne.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lingyun of Qinghe, a staff officer of the Chief Office, dreamed the Lord on High told him: 「Xiao Daocheng is my nineteenth son; last year I already granted him the Son of Heaven’s throne.

sentences.zh: 」自三皇五帝至齊受命君，凡十九人也。

translations.literal: From the Three August Ones and Five Thearchs down to Qi’s recipient of the mandate, there have been nineteen such rulers.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three August Ones and Five Thearchs down to Qi’s recipient of the mandate, there have been nineteen such rulers.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始中，童謠云「東城出天子」，故明帝殺建安王休仁。

translations.literal: In Song Taishi, a children’s rhyme said 「From the eastern city a Son of Heaven will arise,」 so Emperor Ming killed Prince Jian’an Xiuren.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Taishi, a children’s rhyme said 「From the eastern city a Son of Heaven will arise,」 so Emperor Ming killed Prince Jian’an Xiuren.

sentences.zh: 蘇偘云：「後從帝自東城卽位，論者謂應之，乃是武進縣上所居東城里也。

translations.literal: Su Kan said: 「Later the deposed emperor enthroned himself from the eastern city—commentators took this as fulfillment; but it was the eastern city ward where our sovereign’s clan dwelt in Wujin county.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kan said: 「Later the deposed emperor enthroned himself from the eastern city—commentators took this as fulfillment; but it was the eastern city ward where our sovereign’s clan dwelt in Wujin county.

sentences.zh: 」熊襄云：「上舊鄉有大道，相傳云秦始皇所經，呼爲『天子路』，後遂爲帝鄉焉。

translations.literal: 」Xiong Xiang said: 「In the sovereign’s old homeland there is a great road that tradition says Qin Shihuang traveled—called 『the Son of Heaven’s Road』—and it later became the imperial clan’s homeland.
translations.idiomatic: 」Xiong Xiang said: 「In the sovereign’s old homeland there is a great road that tradition says Qin Shihuang traveled—called 『the Son of Heaven’s Road』—and it later became the imperial clan’s homeland.

sentences.zh: 」案從帝實當援立，猶如晉之懷、愍，亦有徵符。

translations.literal: 」The record: the deposed emperor was indeed the rightful successor, like Jin’s Huai and Min—there were portents for him too.
translations.idiomatic: 」On examination, the deposed emperor was indeed the rightful successor, like Jin’s Huai and Min—there were portents for him too.

sentences.zh: 齊運旣無，巡幸路名，或是秦舊，疑不能詳。

translations.literal: With Qi’s fortune already assured, the road name for imperial tours may be a Qin relic—the doubt cannot be settled in detail.
translations.idiomatic: With Qi’s fortune already assured, the road name for imperial tours may be a Qin relic—the point cannot be settled in detail.

sentences.zh: 世祖年十三，夢舉體生毛，髮生至足。

translations.literal: At thirteen Shizu dreamed his whole body sprouted hair, hair growing down to his feet.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Shizu dreamed his whole body sprouted hair, hair growing down to his feet.

sentences.zh: 又夢人指上所踐地曰「周文王之田」。

translations.literal: He also dreamed someone pointed to the ground the sovereign trod and said, 「The fields of King Wen of Zhou.」
translations.idiomatic: He also dreamed someone pointed to the ground the sovereign trod and said, 「The fields of King Wen of Zhou.」

sentences.zh: 又夢虛空中飛。

translations.literal: Again he dreamed of flying in the empty sky.
translations.idiomatic: He also dreamed that he was flying through the empty sky.

sentences.zh: 又夢著孔雀羽衣。

translations.literal: Again he dreamed of wearing peacock-feather garments.
translations.idiomatic: He also dreamed that he was clad in peacock-feather robes.

sentences.zh: 庾溫云：「雀，爵位也。

translations.literal: Yu Wen said: 「The sparrow signifies rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen said: 「The sparrow signifies rank and title.

sentences.zh: 」又夢鳳皇從天飛下青溪宅齋前，兩翅相去十餘丈，翼下有紫雲氣。

translations.literal: 」Again he dreamed that a phoenix flew down from heaven before the study at his Qingxi residence, its two wings spanning more than ten zhang, with purple cloud vapor beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: 」He also dreamed that a phoenix flew down from heaven before the study at his Qingxi residence, its wings spanning more than ten zhang apart, with purple cloud vapor beneath them.

sentences.zh: 及在襄陽，夢著桑屐行度太極殿階。

translations.literal: When he was at Xiangyang, he dreamed of wearing mulberry-wood clogs and walking up the steps of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: While at Xiangyang, he dreamed of wearing mulberry-wood clogs and walking up the steps of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 庾溫云：「屐者，運應木也。

translations.literal: Yu Wen said: 「Clogs signify the fortune of the Wood phase.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen said: 「Clogs signify the fortune of the Wood phase.

sentences.zh: 」臣案桑字爲四十而二點，世祖年過此卽帝位，謂著屐爲木行也。

translations.literal: 」This subject observes that the character sang has forty-two brush strokes; when Emperor Shizu passed that age he would attain the throne—wearing clogs thus signified the Wood phase.
translations.idiomatic: 」I observe that the character for mulberry (sang) contains forty-two strokes; when Emperor Shizu passed that age he would take the throne—so wearing clogs signified the Wood phase.

sentences.zh: 屐有兩齒有聲，是爲明兩之齒至四十二而行卽真矣。

translations.literal: Clogs have two teeth that make a sound—this signifies the paired brightness of the two teeth; at forty-two he would walk forth and become the true sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Clogs have two teeth that click as one walks—an omen of paired brightness; at forty-two he would go forth and become the true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 及在郢州，夢人從天飛下，頭插筆來畫上衣兩邊，不言而去。

translations.literal: When he was at Ying Province, he dreamed of a man flying down from heaven with a brush stuck in his hair, who came to paint both sides of his upper garment and departed without a word.
translations.idiomatic: While at Ying Province, he dreamed of a man flying down from heaven with a brush in his hair, who painted both sides of his upper garment and left without speaking.

sentences.zh: 庾溫釋云：「畫者，山龍華蟲也。」

translations.literal: Yu Wen explained: 「Painting signifies the mountain dragon and flowery creatures.」
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen explained: 「Painting signifies the mountain dragon and flowery creatures [on ceremonial robes].」

sentences.zh: 世祖宋元嘉十七年六月己未夜生，無火，婢吹灰而火自燃。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu was born on the night of the jiwei day in the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Yuanjia; there was no fire, but when a maid blew on the ashes, flame sprang up of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu was born on the jiwei night in the sixth month of Yuanjia 17; there was no fire, yet when a maid blew on the ashes, flame sprang up by itself.

sentences.zh: 世祖於南康郡內作伎，有絃無管，於是空中有篪聲，調節相應。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu was performing entertainments within Nankang commandery, there were strings but no pipes—then from the empty sky came the sound of a chi flute, its modulation answering in tune.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shizu was staging entertainments in Nankang commandery, there were strings but no pipes—then from the empty sky came the sound of a chi flute, perfectly in tune.

sentences.zh: 世祖爲廣興相，嶺下積旱水涸不通船，上部伍至，水忽暴長。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu was administrator of Guangxing, drought had long piled up below the ranges and the waters dried so that boats could not pass; when the upper fifth convoy arrived, the water suddenly swelled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu was administrator of Guangxing, prolonged drought below the ranges had dried the waters and blocked shipping; when the upper fifth convoy arrived, the water suddenly rose in flood.

sentences.zh: 庾溫云：「易利涉大川之義也。」

translations.literal: Yu Wen said: 「This is the meaning of the Changes, “Favorable to cross the great stream.”」
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wen said: 「This is the meaning of the Changes line, “Favorable to cross the great stream.”」

sentences.zh: 世祖頓盆城，城內無水，欲鑿引江流，試掘井，得伏泉九處，皆湧出。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu halted at Pencheng, there was no water within the city; wishing to dig and draw in the Yangtze current, he tried sinking wells and obtained nine hidden springs, all of which gushed forth.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu halted at Pencheng, the city had no water; intending to dig channels to the Yangtze, he tried wells and found nine hidden springs, all of which gushed forth.

sentences.zh: 元徽三年，太祖在青溪宅，齋前池中忽揚波起浪，湧水如山，有金石響，須臾有青龍從池中出，左右皆見之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhui, Grand Progenitor was at his Qingxi residence; before the study the pool suddenly raised waves and surging water like a mountain, with a sound of metal and stone; in a moment an azure dragon emerged from the pool, and those on both sides all saw it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 3, Grand Progenitor was at his Qingxi residence; before the study the pool suddenly heaved into waves like a mountain, with a sound of metal and stone; presently an azure dragon rose from the pool, and all on either side saw it.

sentences.zh: 建元四年，青龍見從陽郡清水縣平泉湖中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, an azure dragon appeared in Pingquan Lake in Qingshui county, Congyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 4, an azure dragon appeared in Pingquan Lake, Qingshui county, Congyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，黃龍見曲江縣黃池中，一宿二日。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming, a yellow dragon appeared in Huangchi, Qujiang county, and remained one night and two days.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 7, a yellow dragon appeared in Huangchi, Qujiang county, and stayed one night and two days.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，山上雲障四塞，頃有玄黃五色如龍，長十餘丈，從西北升天。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing, clouds on the mountain walled in on all four sides; presently there was a dragon of black, yellow, and five colors more than ten zhang long, which ascended to heaven from the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongxing 2, clouds on the mountain shut in the view on every side; presently a dragon of black, yellow, and five colors, more than ten zhang long, rose to heaven from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始末，武進舊塋有獸見，一角，羊頭，龍翼，馬足，父老咸見，莫之識也。

translations.literal: At the end of Song Taishi, a beast appeared at the old tomb mound in Wujin—one horn, a goat's head, dragon wings, and horse's feet; the elders all saw it but none could identify it.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Song Taishi, a beast appeared at the old tomb mound in Wujin—one horn, a goat's head, dragon wings, and horse's feet; the elders all saw it, but none could name it.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，鄱陽郡獻一角獸，麟首，鹿形，龍鸞共色。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming, Poyang commandery presented a one-horned beast with a qilin head, deer form, and the shared hues of dragon and phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 10, Poyang commandery presented a one-horned beast with a qilin head, deer body, and the mingled colors of dragon and phoenix.

sentences.zh: 瑞應圖云：「天子萬福允集，則一角獸至。」

translations.literal: The Records of Auspicious Responses says: 「When the Son of Heaven's myriad blessings are gathered, the one-horned beast arrives.」
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Auspicious Responses says: 「When the Son of Heaven's myriad blessings are gathered, the one-horned beast arrives.」

sentences.zh: 十一年，白象九頭見武昌。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, nine white elephants appeared at Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, nine white elephants appeared at Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：《記》云，升中于天，麟鳳至而龜龍格。

translations.literal: The historian writes: The Records say, “When one ascends and offers in the center to Heaven, the qilin and phoenix arrive and the turtle and dragon come forth.”
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The Records say, “When one ascends and offers in the center to Heaven, the qilin and phoenix arrive and the turtle and dragon come forth.”

sentences.zh: 則鳳皇巢乎阿閣，麒麟在乎郊藪，豈非馴之在庭，擾以成畜，其爲瑞也如此。

translations.literal: Then the phoenix nests in the Aqueous Chamber, the qilin is in the suburban marshes—are they not tamed in the courtyard and accustomed until they become livestock? Such is their character as omens.
translations.idiomatic: Then the phoenix nests in the Aqueous Chamber and the qilin ranges in the suburban marshes—are they not tamed in the courtyard and reared until they become domestic beasts? Such is their nature as portents.

sentences.zh: 今觀魏、晉已來，世稱靈物不少，而亂多治少，史不絕書。

translations.literal: Now observing from Wei and Jin onward, the age has proclaimed no few numinous creatures, yet disorder has been plentiful and good order scarce—the histories never cease recording them.
translations.idiomatic: Looking from Wei and Jin onward, the age has proclaimed no few numinous creatures, yet disorder has been plentiful and good order scarce—the histories never cease recording them.

sentences.zh: 故知來儀在沼，遠非前事，見而不至，未辨其爲祥也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the coming of ceremony at the marsh is far from the events of old; to see and yet not arrive is not yet to distinguish it as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that the phoenix omen at the marsh is far from the events of old; to see and yet not arrive is not yet to know it for a true auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年三月，白虎見歷陽龍亢縣新昌村。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Shengming, a white tiger appeared at Xinchang village, Longkang county, Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Shengming 3, a white tiger appeared at Xinchang village, Longkang county, Liyang.

sentences.zh: 新昌村，嘉名也。

translations.literal: Xinchang village—a felicitous name.
translations.idiomatic: Xinchang village—a felicitous name.

sentences.zh: 《瑞應圖》云：「王者不暴白虎仁。」

translations.literal: The Records of Auspicious Responses says: 「When the king is not cruel, the white tiger appears as benevolence.」
translations.idiomatic: The Records of Auspicious Responses says: 「When the king is not cruel, the white tiger appears as benevolence.」

sentences.zh: 建元四年三月，白虎見安蠻虔化縣。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Jianyuan, a white tiger appeared at Qianhua county, Anman.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Jianyuan 4, a white tiger appeared at Qianhua county, Anman.

sentences.zh: 中興二年二月，白虎見東平壽張安樂村。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhongxing, a white tiger appeared at Anle village, Shouzhang, Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhongxing 2, a white tiger appeared at Anle village, Shouzhang, Dongping.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，騶虞見安東縣五界山，師子頭，虎身，龍脚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, a zouyu appeared at Wujie Mountain, Andong county—a lion's head, tiger's body, and dragon's feet.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2, a zouyu appeared at Wujie Mountain, Andong county—with a lion's head, tiger's body, and dragon's feet.

sentences.zh: 《詩傳》云：「騶虞，義獸，白虎黑文，不食生物，至德則出。」

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Odes says: 「The zouyu is a beast of righteousness, a white tiger with black markings; it does not eat living creatures and appears when supreme virtue is attained.」
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Odes says: 「The zouyu is a beast of righteousness, a white tiger with black markings; it does not eat living creatures and appears when supreme virtue is attained.」

sentences.zh: 昇明三年，太祖爲齊王，白毛龜見東府城池中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming, when Grand Progenitor was Prince of Qi, a white-haired turtle appeared in the moat of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 3, when Grand Progenitor was Prince of Qi, a white-haired turtle appeared in the moat of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，休安陵獲玄龜一頭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, a dark turtle was obtained at the Xiuan Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 2, a dark turtle was obtained at the Xiuan Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，武騎常侍唐潛上青毛神龜一頭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, Palace Attendant for Martial Cavaliers Tang Qian presented a blue-haired divine turtle.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 5, Palace Attendant for Martial Cavaliers Tang Qian presented a blue-haired divine turtle.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，彭城郡田中獲青毛龜一頭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the seventh year, a blue-haired turtle was obtained in the fields of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year, a blue-haired turtle was obtained in the fields of Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 八月，延陵縣前澤畔獲毫龜一枚。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, a downy turtle was obtained on the bank of the marsh before Yanling county.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, a downy turtle was obtained on the bank of the marsh before Yanling county.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，長山縣王惠獲六目龜一頭，腹下有「萬歡」字，幷有卦兆。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Wang Hui of Changshan county obtained a six-eyed turtle; on its belly were the characters “Myriad rejoicing,” together with hexagram omens.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year, Wang Hui of Changshan county obtained a six-eyed turtle; on its belly were the characters “Myriad rejoicing,” together with hexagram omens.

sentences.zh: 六月，建城縣昌城田獲四目龜一頭，下有「萬齊」字。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, a four-eyed turtle was obtained in the fields of Changcheng, Jiancheng county; on its underside were the characters “Myriad Qi.”
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, a four-eyed turtle was obtained in the fields of Changcheng, Jiancheng county; on its underside were the characters “Myriad Qi.”

sentences.zh: 九年五月，長山縣獲神龜一頭，腹下有《巽兌》卦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year, a divine turtle was obtained in Changshan county; on its belly was the hexagram Xun over Dui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year, a divine turtle was obtained in Changshan county; on its belly was the hexagram Xun over Dui.

sentences.zh: 中興二年正月，邏將潘道蓋於山石穴中獲毛龜一頭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhongxing, the frontier commander Pan Daogai obtained a downy turtle in a mountain rock cave.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhongxing 2, the frontier commander Pan Daogai obtained a downy turtle in a mountain rock cave.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年，世祖遣人詣宮亭湖廟還福，船泊渚，有白魚雙躍入船。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming, Emperor Shizu sent men to the Gongting Lake shrine to return thanks for blessings; when the boat moored at the islet, a pair of white fish leaped together into the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 3, Emperor Shizu sent men to the Gongting Lake shrine to return thanks for blessings; when the boat moored at the islet, a pair of white fish leaped together into the vessel.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，南豫州刺史建安王子真表獻金色魚一頭。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, the Prince of Jian'an, Zizhen, as Governor of South Yuzhou, memorialized and presented a golden fish.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 5, the Prince of Jian'an, Zizhen, as Governor of South Yuzhou, memorialized and presented a golden fish.

sentences.zh: 建元元年八月，男子王約獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Jianyuan, the commoner Wang Yue obtained a white magpie.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Jianyuan 1, the commoner Wang Yue obtained a white magpie.

sentences.zh: 九月，秣陵縣獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Moling county obtained a white magpie.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Moling county obtained a white magpie.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，白雀集郢州府館。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, white magpies gathered at the Ying Province government hostel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year, white magpies gathered at the Ying Province government hostel.

sentences.zh: 五月，白雀見會稽永興縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, a white magpie appeared at Yongxing county, Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, a white magpie appeared at Yongxing county, Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 永明元年五月，郢州丁坡屯獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongming, Dingpo garrison in Ying Province obtained a white magpie.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongming 1, Dingpo garrison in Ying Province obtained a white magpie.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，安城王暠第獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the third year, seventh month, at Prince of Ancheng Gao's residence a white sparrow was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, a white sparrow was obtained at the residence of Prince of Ancheng Gao.

sentences.zh: 九月，南郡江陵縣獲白雀一頭

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Jiangling county in Nan commandery obtained one white sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Jiangling county in Nan commandery obtained a white sparrow.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，白雀見臨汝縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, seventh month, a white sparrow appeared in Linru county.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year, a white sparrow appeared in Linru county.

sentences.zh: 七年六月，鹽官縣獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, sixth month, Yanguan county obtained one white sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the seventh year, Yanguan county obtained a white sparrow.

sentences.zh: 八年，天門臨澧縣獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Linli county in Tianmen obtained one white sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, Linli county in Tianmen obtained a white sparrow.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，吳郡錢塘縣獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, seventh month, Qiantang county in Wu commandery obtained one white sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the ninth year, Qiantang county in Wu commandery obtained a white sparrow.

sentences.zh: 八月，豫州獲白雀一頭

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yuzhou obtained one white sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Yuzhou obtained a white sparrow.

sentences.zh: 十年五月，齊郡獲白雀一頭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, fifth month, Qi commandery obtained one white sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the tenth year, Qi commandery obtained a white sparrow.

sentences.zh: 建元元年五月，白烏見巴郡。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jianyuan, a white crow appeared in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jianyuan 1, a white crow appeared in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 永明四年三月，三足烏巢南安中陶縣庭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, third month, a three-legged crow nested in the courtyard of Zhongtao county in Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongming 4, a three-legged crow nested in the courtyard of Zhongtao county in Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，陽羨縣獲白烏一頭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, eighth month, Yangxian county obtained one white crow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year, Yangxian county obtained a white crow.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年四月，陽羨縣獲白烏一頭。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Longchang, Yangxian county obtained one white crow.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Longchang 1, Yangxian county obtained a white crow.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，江陵縣獲白鼠一頭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, Jiangling county obtained one white rat.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 2, Jiangling county obtained a white rat.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，白鼠見芳林園。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming, a white rat appeared in Fanglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 6, a white rat appeared in Fanglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 十年九月，義陽郡獲白鼠一頭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, ninth month, Yiyang commandery obtained one white rat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the tenth year, Yiyang commandery obtained a white rat.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，丹楊縣獲白兔一頭。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, Danyang county obtained one white hare.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 4, Danyang county obtained a white hare.

sentences.zh: 昇明元年六月，慶雲見益都。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Shengming, auspicious clouds appeared at Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Shengming 1, auspicious clouds appeared at Yidu.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，世祖拜皇太子日，有慶雲在日邊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, on the day the Founding Emperor was invested as crown prince, auspicious clouds appeared beside the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan 1, on the day the Founding Emperor was made crown prince, auspicious clouds appeared beside the sun.

sentences.zh: 三年，華林園醴泉堂東忽有瑞雲，周圓十許丈，高下與景雲樓平，五色藻密，光彩映山，徘徊良久，行轉南行，過長船入華池。

translations.literal: In the third year, east of the Sweet Spring Hall in Fanglin Garden there suddenly appeared an auspicious cloud, about ten zhang in circumference, level in height with the Jingyun tower, dense with five colors, its brilliance reflected on the mountains; it lingered long, then shifted south, passed the Long Ship and entered Huachi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an auspicious cloud suddenly appeared east of the Sweet Spring Hall in Fanglin Garden—some ten zhang around, level with the Jingyun tower, thick with five colors and light flashing on the hills. It hovered a long while, then drifted south, passed the Long Ship, and entered Huachi.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，宣城臨成縣於藉山獲紫芝一枝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, Lincheng county in Xuancheng obtained one sprig of purple fungus on Jie mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 2, Lincheng county in Xuancheng obtained a sprig of purple fungus on Jie mountain.

sentences.zh: 永明八年五月，陽城縣獲紫芝一株。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year of Yongming, Yangcheng county obtained one plant of purple fungus.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongming 8, Yangcheng county obtained a plant of purple fungus.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年正月，襄陽縣獲紫芝一莖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Longchang, Xiangyang county obtained one stalk of purple fungus.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Longchang 1, Xiangyang county obtained a stalk of purple fungus.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年四月，昌國縣徐萬年門下棠樹連理。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Shengming, at Xu Wannian's gate in Changguo county, crabapple trees grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Shengming 2, crabapple trees at Xu Wannian's gate in Changguo county grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 九月，豫州萬歲澗廣數丈，有樹連理，隔澗騰枝相通，越壑跨水爲一榦。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, at Wansui Brook in Yuzhou, several zhang wide, trees grew interlocking; branches leapt the stream and joined across ravines and water into one trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, at Wansui Brook in Yuzhou—several zhang across—trees grew interlocking, their branches spanning the stream and merging over gullies and water into a single trunk.

sentences.zh: 建元二年九月，有司奏上虞縣楓樹連理，兩根相去九尺，雙株均聳，去地九尺，合成一榦。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Jianyuan, the authorities reported that maple trees in Shangyu county grew interlocking, the two roots nine chi apart, the paired trunks rising evenly nine chi from the ground and merging into one trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Jianyuan 2, officials reported interlocking maples in Shangyu county: two roots nine chi apart, twin stems rising evenly nine chi from the ground and fusing into one trunk.

sentences.zh: 故鄣縣楓樹連理，兩株相去七尺，大八圍，去地一丈，仍相合爲樹，泯如一木。

translations.literal: In Guzhang county maple trees grew interlocking, the two trunks seven chi apart, eight arm-spans around, one zhang from the ground they joined into one tree, indistinguishable as a single wood.
translations.idiomatic: In Guzhang county interlocking maples stood seven chi apart, eight arm-spans around; one zhang above ground they fused into one tree, as if a single trunk.

sentences.zh: 山陽縣界若邪村有一槻木，合爲連理。

translations.literal: At Ruoye village on the border of Shanyang county there was one zelkova whose parts joined in interlocking growth.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruoye village on the border of Shanyang county a zelkova grew with joined interlocking parts.

sentences.zh: 淮陰縣建業寺梨樹連理。

translations.literal: Pear trees at Jianye Temple in Huaiyin county grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: Pear trees at Jianye Temple in Huaiyin county grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 建康縣梨樹耀欀一本作耀攘五圍，連理六枝。

translations.literal: Pear trees in Jiankang county, yao rao (one text reads yao rang), five arm-spans around, with six interlocking branches.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiankang county pear trees—yao rao (one text reads yao rang)—five arm-spans around, bore six interlocking branches.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，烏程縣陳文則家槿樹連理。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year, at Chen Wenzhe's home in Wucheng county, hibiscus trees grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year, hibiscus trees at Chen Wenzhe's home in Wucheng county grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 七月，新冶縣槐栗二木合生異根連理，去地數尺，中央小開，上復爲一。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, in Xinye county locust and chestnut trees grew together with separate roots interlocking, several chi from the ground; the center opened slightly, then above became one.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, in Xinye county locust and chestnut trees merged from separate interlocking roots a few chi above ground; the center gaped slightly, then closed into one above.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，安城縣榆樹二株連理。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, two elm trees in Ancheng county grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, two elm trees in Ancheng county grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 二月，安陽縣梓樹連理。

translations.literal: In the second month, catalpa trees in Anyang county grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, catalpa trees in Anyang county grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 九月，句陽縣之糓山槿樹連理，異根雙挺，共杪爲一。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, hibiscus trees on Gushan in Gouyang county grew interlocking, with separate roots twin-standing, their tips joined as one.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, hibiscus on Gushan in Gouyang county grew interlocking—twin roots, separate below, one crown above.

sentences.zh: 十二月，永寧左郡樠木連理。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, trees in Yongning Left Commandery grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, trees in Yongning Left Commandery grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，秣陵縣喬天明園中李樹連理生，高三尺五寸，兩枝別生，復高三尺，合爲一榦。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, in Qiao Tianming's garden in Moling county a plum tree grew interlocking, three chi five cun high; two branches sprouted apart, rose another three chi, and merged into one trunk.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, in Qiao Tianming's garden in Moling county an interlocking plum stood three chi five cun tall; two branches parted, rose three chi more, and fused into one trunk.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，秣陵縣華僧秀園中四樹連理。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, four trees in Hua Sengxiu's garden in Moling county grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, four trees in Hua Sengxiu's garden in Moling county grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，江寧縣北界賴鄉齊平里三成邏門外路東太常蕭惠基園楥樹二株連理，其高相去二尺，南大北小，小者傾柯南附，合爲一樹，枝葉繁茂，圓密如蓋。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the sixth year, two zelkova trees in Director of Ceremonies Xiao Huiji's garden east of the road outside Sancheng Luo Gate at Qiping li, Laixiang on the northern border of Jiangning county, grew interlocking; their heights two chi apart, the southern larger and the northern smaller, the smaller leaning and leaning on the larger until they merged into one tree, foliage lush and round-dense as a canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the sixth year, two zelkova in Director of Ceremonies Xiao Huiji's garden east of the road outside Sancheng Luo Gate, Qiping li, Laixiang on Jiangning's northern border, grew interlocking two chi apart—the southern trunk larger, the northern smaller, the smaller leaning into the larger until they became one tree, foliage thick and round as a canopy.

sentences.zh: 七年，江寧縣李樹二株連理，兩根相去一丈五尺。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, two plum trees in Jiangning county grew interlocking, the two roots one zhang five chi apart.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, two plum trees in Jiangning county grew with joined trunks, their roots one zhang five chi apart.

sentences.zh: 八年，巴陵郡樹連理四株。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, four trees in Baling commandery grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, four trees in Baling commandery grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 三月，武陵白沙戍槻木連理，相去五尺，俱高三尺，東西二枝，合而通柯。

translations.literal: In the third month, zelkova at Baisha garrison in Wuling grew interlocking, five chi apart, each three chi high; east and west branches merged with connected boughs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, zelkova at Baisha garrison in Wuling grew interlocking five chi apart and three chi tall; eastern and western branches fused with shared boughs.

sentences.zh: 十二月，柴桑縣陶委天家樹連理。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, trees at Tao Weitian's home in Chaisang county grew interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, trees at Tao Weitian's home in Chaisang county grew with joined trunks.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，山陰縣孔廣家園檉樹十二層。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, a tamarisk in Kong Guang's garden in Shanyin county had twelve tiers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 5, a tamarisk in Kong Guang's garden in Shanyin county bore twelve tiers.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守隨王子隆獻之，種芳林園鳳光殿西。

translations.literal: Kuaiji Administrator Sui, Prince of Zi, presented it; it was planted west of the Phoenix Light Hall in Fanglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji Administrator Sui, Prince of Zi, presented it; it was planted west of the Phoenix Light Hall in Fanglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 九年，秣陵縣鬭場里安明寺有古樹，衆僧改架屋宇，伐以爲薪，剖樹木裏，自然有「法大德」三字。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at Anming Temple in Douchang li, Moling county, there was an old tree; the monks rebuilt the hall and felled it for firewood; when the tree was split, the characters Fa Da De ("Dharma of Great Virtue") appeared naturally in the wood.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at Anming Temple in Douchang li, Moling county, monks rebuilding the hall cut an old tree for firewood; inside the split wood the characters Fa Da De ("Dharma of Great Virtue") appeared of themselves.

sentences.zh: 始興郡本無欓樹，調味有闕。

translations.literal: Shixing commandery originally had no litsea trees, and seasonings were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing commandery had no litsea trees, so condiments were wanting.

sentences.zh: 世祖在郡，堂屋後忽生一株。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was in the commandery, one suddenly grew behind the hall.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founding Emperor governed the commandery, one suddenly sprang up behind the hall.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年十月，甘露降建康縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Shengming, sweet dew fell in Jiankang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Shengming 2, sweet dew fell in Jiankang county.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甘露降長山縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, sweet dew fell in Changshan county.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, sweet dew fell in Changshan county.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甘露降彭山松樹，至九日止。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, sweet dew fell on pines at Peng mountain until the ninth day ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, sweet dew fell on pines at Peng mountain and continued until the ninth day.

sentences.zh: 建元元年九月，甘露降淮南郡桃石榴二樹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jianyuan, sweet dew fell on peach and pomegranate trees in Huainan commandery—two trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Jianyuan 1, sweet dew fell on two trees in Huainan commandery—a peach and a pomegranate.

sentences.zh: 有司奏甘露降新汲縣王安世園樹。

translations.literal: The authorities reported sweet dew falling on trees in Wang Anshi's garden in Xinji county.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported sweet dew on the trees in Wang Anshi's garden in Xinji county.

sentences.zh: 永明二年四月，甘露降南郡桐樹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yongming, sweet dew fell on paulownia in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongming 2, sweet dew fell on paulownia in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，甘露降臨湘縣李樹。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, sweet dew fell on plum trees in Linxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, sweet dew fell on plum trees in Linxiang county.

sentences.zh: 三月，甘露降南郡桐樹。

translations.literal: In the third month, sweet dew fell on paulownia in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, sweet dew fell on paulownia in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 四月，甘露降睢陽縣桃樹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, sweet dew fell on peach trees in Suiyang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, sweet dew fell on peach trees in Suiyang county.

sentences.zh: 五年四月，甘露降荊州府中閤外桐樹。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year, sweet dew fell on paulownia outside the central pavilion of Jingzhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year, sweet dew fell on paulownia outside the inner gate of Jingzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，甘露降芳林園故山堂桐樹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, sweet dew fell on paulownia at the Old Mountain Hall in Fanglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, sweet dew fell on paulownia at the Old Mountain Hall in Fanglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 九年八月，甘露降上定林寺佛堂庭，中天如雨，徧地如雪，其氣芳，其味甘，耀日舞風，至晡乃止。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year, sweet dew fell in the Buddha hall court of Upper Dinglin Temple; from mid-heaven it rained down, spreading over the ground like snow—fragrant on the air, sweet on the tongue, glittering in sunlight and swirling in the wind, until dusk it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the ninth year, sweet dew fell in the Buddha hall court of Upper Dinglin Temple—from mid-heaven it poured, the ground white as snow, the air fragrant, the taste sweet, light dancing in sun and wind until dusk.

sentences.zh: 爾後頻降鍾山松樹，四十餘日乃止。

translations.literal: After that it fell often on pines at Zhong mountain, and did not cease for more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: After that it fell again and again on pines at Zhong mountain, and for more than forty days did not stop.

sentences.zh: 十月，甘露降太安陵樹。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, sweet dew fell on trees at Tai'an Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, sweet dew fell on trees at Tai'an Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 中興二年三月，甘露降茅山，彌漫數里。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Zhongxing, sweet dew fell on Maoshan, spreading for several li.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhongxing 2, sweet dew fell on Maoshan and spread for several li.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年三月，醴泉出昌國白鹿山，其味甚甘。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Yuanhui, sweet spring water issued from Bailu mountain in Changguo; its taste was very sweet.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yuanhui 4, sweet spring water welled up on Bailu mountain in Changguo, and its taste was surpassingly sweet.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，梁郡睢陽縣界野田中獲嘉禾，一莖二十三穗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year, in the border wild fields of Suiyang county in Liang commandery, auspicious grain was obtained—one stalk with twenty-three ears.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year, in wild fields on the border of Suiyang county in Liang commandery, men found auspicious grain—one stalk bearing twenty-three ears.

sentences.zh: 五年九月，莒縣獲嘉禾一株。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fifth year, Ju county obtained one stalk of auspicious grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fifth year, Ju county obtained a stalk of auspicious grain.

sentences.zh: 十年六月，海陵齊昌縣獲嘉禾，一莖六穗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year, Qichang county in Hailing obtained auspicious grain—one stalk with six ears.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the tenth year, Qichang county in Hailing obtained auspicious grain—one stalk with six ears.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，睢陽縣田中獲嘉禾一株。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, one stalk of auspicious grain was obtained in the fields of Suiyang county.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year, a stalk of auspicious grain was found in the fields of Suiyang county.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年九月，建寧縣建昌村民採藥於萬歲山，忽聞澗中有異響，得銅鍾一枚，長二尺一寸，邊有古字。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Shengming, villagers of Jianchang in Jianning county were gathering herbs on Wansui mountain; they suddenly heard a strange sound in the brook and obtained one bronze bell, two chi one cun long, with ancient characters on its rim.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Shengming 2, Jianchang villagers in Jianning county were gathering herbs on Wansui mountain when a strange sound rose from the stream—they drew up a bronze bell two chi one cun long, its rim marked with ancient characters.

sentences.zh: 建元元年十月，涪陵郡蜑民田健所住巖間，常留雲氣，有聲響澈若龍吟，求之積歲，莫有見者。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Jianyuan, in the cliff where Tiao tribesman Tian Jian of Fuling commandery lived, cloud and mist often lingered, and sounds rang clear like a dragon's cry; for years men sought the source, yet none saw it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Jianyuan 1, at the cliff where Tiao tribesman Tian Jian of Fuling commandery dwelt, mist always hung and a sound rang through like dragon-song; men searched year after year and never saw its source.

sentences.zh: 去四月二十七日，巖數里夜忽有雙光，至明往，獲古鍾一枚，又有一器名淳于，蜑人以爲神物奉祠之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month past, several li from the cliff twin lights appeared by night; at dawn they went and obtained an ancient bell, and also a vessel called Chunyu; the Tiao people regarded them as divine objects and offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh of the fourth month past, twin lights flared in the night several li from the cliff; at dawn men went and found an ancient bell and a vessel called Chunyu—the Tiao people took them for sacred things and set them up for worship.

sentences.zh: 永明四年四月，東昌縣山自比歲以來，恒發異響，去二月十五日，有一巖褫落，縣民方元泰往視，於巖下得古鍾一枚。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yongming, since this year the mountain in Dongchang county had constantly given strange sounds; on the fifteenth day of the second month past a cliff-face peeled away, and county resident Fang Yuantai went to see; beneath the cliff he obtained an ancient bell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongming 4, the mountain in Dongchang county had given strange sounds all that year; on the fifteenth of the second month past a cliff sloughed away, and Fang Yuantai of the county went to look—beneath the rock he found an ancient bell.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，豫寧縣長崗山獲神鍾一枚。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, Changgang mountain in Yuning county obtained a divine bell.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, a divine bell was found on Changgang mountain in Yuning county.

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，寧蜀廣漢縣田所墾地入尺四寸，獲古鍾一枚，形高三尺八寸，圍四尺七寸，縣柄長一尺二寸，合高五尺，四面各九孔。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, in the fields of Ningsu Guanghan county, while plowing at one chi four cun depth, an ancient bell was obtained—three chi eight cun high, four chi seven cun around, the suspension loop one chi two cun, total height five chi, nine holes on each of four sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, plowing fields in Ningsu Guanghan county, men struck an ancient bell one chi four cun down—three chi eight cun tall, four chi seven cun around, the loop one chi two cun, five chi in all, nine holes on each face.

sentences.zh: 更於陶所瓦間見有白光，窺尋無物，自後夜夜輙復有光，旣經旬日，村民張慶宣瓦作屋，又於屋間見光照內外，慶宣疑之，以告孔休先，乃共發視，獲玉璽一鈕，璧方八分，上有鼻，文曰「帝真」。

translations.literal: Again, among the pottery tiles white light was seen; they peered and found nothing. After that each night light appeared again; after ten days had passed, villager Zhang Qingxuan built a tile house, and again light shone inside and outside the house. Qingxuan grew suspicious and told Kong Xiuxian; together they dug and obtained a jade seal knob, the bi one cun square, with a nose, inscribed Di Zhen ("True Emperor").
translations.idiomatic: Again white light showed between the kiln tiles; they looked and found nothing. Night after night the light returned, and after ten days Zhang Qingxuan roofed the spot with tiles—then light filled the hut inside and out. Suspicious, he told Kong Xiuxian; together they opened the ground and found a jade seal knob, a bi one cun square with a nose, inscribed Di Zhen ("True Emperor").

sentences.zh: 曲阿縣民黃慶宅左有園，園東南廣袤四丈，每種菜，輙鮮異，雖加採拔，隨復更生。

translations.literal: Huang Qing of Qu'a county had a garden to the left of his home; southeast of the garden, four zhang in length and breadth—whenever vegetables were planted they were peculiarly fresh and strange; though cut and picked, they regrew at once.
translations.idiomatic: To the left of Huang Qing's house in Qu'a county stood a garden four zhang across on the southeast—whatever he planted grew oddly lush, and though he cut and cut again, it sprang back at once.

sentences.zh: 夜中恒有白光，皎質屬天，狀似縣絹，私疑非常，請師卜候，道士傅德占使掘之，深三尺，獲玉印一鈕，文曰「長承萬福」。

translations.literal: At night white light always appeared, bright quality reaching heaven, shaped like hanging silk; privately he suspected it extraordinary and asked a master to divine; the Daoist Fu Dezhan had them dig—at three chi depth they obtained a jade seal knob inscribed Chang Cheng Wan Fu ("Long succession, myriad blessings").
translations.idiomatic: By night white light always shone, bright as if it touched the sky, like silk hung in air; he took it for a marvel and called a diviner—the Daoist Fu Dezhan bade them dig, and at three chi they found a jade seal knob inscribed Chang Cheng Wan Fu ("Long succession, myriad blessings").

sentences.zh: 永明二年正月，冠軍將軍周普孫於石頭北廂將堂見地有異光照城堞，往獲玉璽一鈕，方七分，文曰「明玄君」。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Yongming, General Who Vanquishes the Enemy Zhou Pusun, at the command post north of Stone City, saw the ground cast strange light on the battlements; he went and obtained a jade seal knob one cun square, inscribed Ming Xuan Jun ("Luminous Mysterious Lord").
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yongming 2, General Who Vanquishes the Enemy Zhou Pusun, in the north wing of the Stone City command post, saw uncanny light on the ramparts; he went and took a jade seal knob one cun square, inscribed Ming Xuan Jun ("Luminous Mysterious Lord").

sentences.zh: 十一月，虜國民齊祥歸入靈丘關，聞殷然有聲，仰視之，見山側有紫氣如雲，衆鳥回翔其間。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Qi Xiang, a subject of the Hu state who had surrendered, entered Lingqiu Pass; he heard a deep rumbling sound, looked up, and saw on the mountainside purple qi like clouds, with many birds wheeling within it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Qi Xiang of the Northern Wei, come over to surrender, entered Lingqiu Pass; a deep sound rolled above him, and on the slope purple vapor gathered like cloud, birds circling within it.

sentences.zh: 祥往氣所，獲璽方寸四分，獸鈕，文曰「坤維聖帝永昌」。

translations.literal: Xiang went to where the qi was and obtained a seal one cun four fen square, with a beast knob, inscribed Kunwei Holy Emperor Eternal Prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang went to the vapor and found a seal one cun four fen square, beast-knobbed, inscribed Kunwei Holy Emperor Eternal Prosperity.

sentences.zh: 送與虜太后師道人惠度，欲獻虜主。

translations.literal: He sent it to the Hu Empress Dowager's monk Hui Du, intending to present it to the Hu ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He sent it to the Hu Empress Dowager's monk Hui Du, meaning to offer it to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 惠度覩其文，竊謂「當今衣冠正朔，在於齊國」。

translations.literal: Hui Du read the inscription and privately said, 「Today the proper succession and orthodox rites lie with the Qi state.」
translations.idiomatic: Hui Du read the text and murmured, 「The true throne and the rites of the cap and gown now belong to Qi.」

sentences.zh: 遂附道人惠藏送京師，因羽林監崔士亮獻之。

translations.literal: He then had the monk Hui Zang escort it to the capital, and through Feathered Forest Supervisor Cui Shiliang it was presented.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the monk Hui Zang with it to the capital, and through Feathered Forest Supervisor Cui Shiliang it reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，始興郡民龔玄宣云，去年二月，忽有一道人乞食，因探懷中出篆書真經一卷，六紙，又表北極一紙，又移付羅漢居士一紙，云從兜率天宮下，使送上天子，因失道人所在。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, Gong Xuanyuan of Shixing commandery reported that in the second month of last year a Daoist suddenly begged food, then drew from his robe a scroll of seal-script true scripture in six sheets, plus one sheet on the North Pole, and one more transferring it to the Arhat layman—saying he came down from Tusita Heaven to have it delivered to the Son of Heaven, then the Daoist vanished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year, Gong Xuanyuan of Shixing commandery said that last second month a Daoist begged for food, then from his robe produced a six-leaf scroll of seal-script scripture, a sheet on the North Pole, and another for the Arhat layman—saying he descended from Tusita Heaven to bring them to the Son of Heaven, and was gone.

sentences.zh: 今年正月，玄宣又稱神人授皇帝璽，龜形，長五寸，廣二寸，厚二寸五分，上有「天地」字，中央「蕭」字，下「萬世」字。

translations.literal: In the first month of this year, Xuanyuan again reported that a spirit-man had bestowed the Emperor's seal, tortoise-shaped, five cun long, two cun wide, two cun five fen thick, with the characters Heaven and Earth above, Xiao at the center, and Myriad Ages below.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of this year Xuanyuan again claimed a spirit had given him the Emperor's seal—tortoise-shaped, five cun long, two cun wide, two cun five fen thick, bearing Heaven and Earth above, Xiao at the center, and Myriad Ages below.

sentences.zh: 十年，蘭陵民齊伯生於六合山獲金璽一鈕，文曰「年予主」。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the commoner Qi Bosheng of Lanling obtained a gold seal knob on Mount Liuhe; the inscription read Nian Yu Zhu ("The year grants the lord").
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Qi Bosheng of Lanling obtained a gold seal knob on Mount Liuhe, inscribed Nian Yu Zhu ("The year grants the lord").

sentences.zh: 世祖治盆城，得五尺刀一十口，永明年曆之數。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu administered Pencheng, he obtained ten five-chi knives—the number of years in the Yongming calendar.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Pencheng, Emperor Shizu found ten five-chi knives—the count of years in the Yongming era.

sentences.zh: 昇明三年，左里村人於宮亭湖得靫戟二枚，傍有古字，文遠不可識。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming, a man of Zuoli village obtained two leather-hilted halberds at Gongting Lake; beside them were ancient characters, the writing too distant to decipher.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming 3, a man of Zuoli village drew two leather-hilted halberds from Gongting Lake; ancient characters lay beside them, too worn to read.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，世祖於青溪宅得錢一枚，文有北斗七星雙節，又有人形帶劔。

translations.literal: During Taishi, Emperor Shizu at his Qingxi residence obtained a coin whose inscription bore the Northern Dipper, seven stars, and two nodes, and also a human form with sword.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era, at his Qingxi residence Emperor Shizu found a coin marked with the Northern Dipper, seven stars, twin nodes, and a sword-bearing human figure.

sentences.zh: 及治盆城，又得一大錢，文曰「太平百歲」。

translations.literal: When he administered Pencheng, he again obtained a large coin inscribed Great Peace for a Hundred Years.
translations.idiomatic: When he governed Pencheng he found another large coin inscribed Great Peace for a Hundred Years.

sentences.zh: 永明七年，齊興太守劉元寶治郡城，於塹中獲錢百萬，形極大，以獻臺爲瑞，世祖班賜朝臣以下各有差。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming, Liu Yuanbao, Administrator of Qixing, while repairing the commandery city, obtained a million coins in the moat—of enormous size; presenting them to the court as an auspicious sign, Emperor Shizu distributed gifts to court ministers and below, each according to rank.
